newsitem.title: ITALY: Opposition wants 1,000 amendments to Italy budget.
newsitem.headline: Opposition wants 1,000 amendments to Italy budget.

text.p: Opposition parties presented some 1,000 amendments on Thursday to the main body of the government's 1997 budget law, increasing the likelihood of a confidence vote in the lower house of parliament.
The amendments would affect around 10 articles of the law which is being voted on article by article in the chamber of deputies. Some 60 articles have already been approved.
Opposition parties are boycotting the budget debate to protest over a far-reaching tax reform.

Fabio Mussi, head of the parliamentary group of the left-wing PDS party, which is the main component of the government coalition, said a confidence vote could be called to get round the filibustering.

The government has said it wants the budget to clear the lower house by Thursday before going to the Senate (upper house) for ratification but political commentators said the lower house debate could spill over into the weekend.
